instruction: I want to teach about double letters. Can you highlight (with background color) all words that contain double letters (like 'll', 'oo', 'tt', etc.)?

command: import pyautogui; import time; pyautogui.hotkey('ctrl', 's'); time.sleep(0.5);

metadata.explanation: Task requires highlighting words with double letters. Verified from word list: 7 words have double letters - all (ll), well (ll), soon (oo), good (oo), pretty (tt), will (ll), too (oo). Evaluator checks for background highlight color on these words.

llm_judge_reasons: Over-strict verification: Evaluator requires words WITHOUT double letters must NOT be highlighted, but instruction only asks to highlight words WITH double letters (doesn't prohibit highlighting others)
Run-level granularity risk: Assumes each run contains exactly one word, but words could span multiple runs or multiple words could be in one run
Punctuation handling: The evaluator strips whitespace but doesn't handle punctuation, so 'all,' and 'all' would be treated as different words
Double letter detection logic is semantically correct (checks consecutive duplicate letters case-insensitively)
Postconfig appropriately saves the document with Ctrl+S to ensure highlight state is persisted
Table structure assumption is reasonable for Dolch word lists
llm_judge_fix_suggestions: Remove the check that fails when non-double-letter words are highlighted (lines 49-53). Only verify that words WITH double letters ARE highlighted.
Add punctuation stripping to word processing (e.g., word.strip().strip('.,;:!?')) before checking for double letters
Consider aggregating runs into complete words before checking, or document the assumption that each run is a complete word
Add logging to show which double-letter words were found and verified, to aid debugging
